To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new method to learn a morphological structure of images, and that this structure is well suited to represent the images in a sparse and non negative way, and that it is equivariant to morphological operators.

we introduce a novel method for online sparse non negative decomposition of data that is based on asymmetric auto encoder, and we demonstrate its effectiveness on a hyperspectral dataset, where the method is able to extract the morphological structure of the data, and we introduce a novel measure of the quality of the decomposition, based on the ability of the representation to approximate morphological operators.

(i) a non negative auto encoder with asymmetric encoder and decoder can learn a part-based representation of a dataset; (ii) such representation is sparse and explainable (iii) this method compares favorably with the state of the arts methods on two benchmark dataset (MNIST and fashion MNIST) and one hyperspectral image.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach for learning a part based representation that is sparse, non negative and explainable.
a new approach to image representation and classification, based on a deep, asymmetric auto encoder and on morphological operators.
the problem of finding an online, sparse, morphological representation for a given image.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method provides a good trade off between the quality of the representation, its interpretability and the speed at which it can be computed.

our method is able to provide a sparse, nonnegative representation of a dataset, that can be computed online for new samples and is equivariant to morphological operators (in the sense that the morphological operator can be computed directly on the representation).

our method is the first one, that we are aware of, that is able to approximate the morphological structure of an image, with a sparse, explainable, non negative representation, computed on the fly, with a low number of iterations, and with a low computational cost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a method to learn an explainable representation for images, that can be computed online for new images and that is equivariant to morphological operators.
we propose a new method that learns a sparse and explainable representation of images, which is equivariant to morphological operations.
we propose an online, part-based morphological representation of images, that is sparse, non negative, explainable and equivariant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the equivariance to morphological operators is a good indicator for a good part based representation.
, by learning a sparse and non negative decomposition of images, one can obtain a part based representation that is explainable, and that is able to encode morphological information.
the proposed method can be used to build a morphological representation of the data that is equivariant to the action of morphological operators.
